content.title: About
content.content: Beef is the meat of cattle, taken from the muscle tissue. Steak cut into cubes is often used in quick‑cook dishes, salads and stir‑fries. The pieces have a tender flavor, moderate fat content and a characteristic meaty texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide.
Cube‑cut steak is popular in dishes like beef stroganoff, kebabs and Asian stir‑fries.
The quality of beef depends heavily on the cattle breed, age and feeding method.
Marbling (intramuscular fat) determines juiciness and flavor.
In many countries certain cuts of beef are considered delicacies, especially tenderloin and ribeye.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Beef provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Heme iron from beef is highly bioavailable and helps prevent anemia.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef is high in B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals are important for immune health and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Creatine
items.content: Natural creatine in beef can aid muscle strength and endurance.

items.title: High in saturated fat
items.content: Excessive intake may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked beef can harbor pathogens such as Salmonella or E. coli.

items.title: Allergy or sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience reactions to beef.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Large amounts can exacerbate gout symptoms.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cube‑cut steak can be quickly seared over high heat, added to stews, soups, salads, or cooked in a teriyaki sauce. Before cooking, trim excess fat and season with salt, pepper and herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0‑4 °C in an airtight container for 3‑5 days. For longer storage freeze at –18 °C, where it remains good for up to 6 months. Thaw in the refrigerator rather than at room temperature.

content.title: About
content.content: The Grilled Chicken Fillet Sandwich is a popular fast‑food item consisting of tender chicken fillet grilled to perfection, fresh vegetables, and a soft bun. It is served hot and often accompanied by a sauce such as mayo or mustard.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The sandwich was introduced to the menu of the fast‑food chain in 2015 as part of the "Grill" line.
The chicken fillet is prepared without breading, reducing fat content compared to traditional chicken nuggets.
Skin‑less chicken breast is used, making the product more diet‑friendly.
The bun is lightly toasted to add a crunchy crust and hold in the fillet juices.
The sandwich is frequently offered with fries and a drink as a combo meal.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken breast provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The lack of breading and skin makes the sandwich less fatty than many other fast‑food options.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken contains niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, supporting metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies phosphorus and selenium, important for bone health and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Vegetable content
items.content: Fresh veggies add fiber, vitamin C and antioxidants.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Sauces and seasonings can increase salt levels, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite lower fat, the sandwich still provides a notable amount of calories due to the bun and sauce.

items.title: Temperature control
items.content: Insufficient cooking of the fillet can pose a risk of bacterial contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the sandwich while hot, immediately after preparation, to keep the bun crisp and the fillet juicy. Add your favorite sauce, lettuce, tomato or cucumber for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The sandwich is best eaten right away. If needed, store in the refrigerator for no more than 2 hours in an airtight container. Reheat in a microwave or on a grill to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

content.title: About
content.content: A ham sandwich or sub is a popular fast‑food item consisting of sliced ham, cheese, vegetables and sauce placed between a split roll or a long bread (sub). Common additions include lettuce, tomato, cucumber, mustard or mayonnaise. It is served in quick‑service restaurants and cafés.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The ham sandwich became popular in the United States in the early 1920s as a convenient work lunch.
The term "sub" (short for "submarine sandwich") comes from the shape of the roll, resembling a submarine.
The ham used is often smoked, giving the sandwich its characteristic aroma.
Regional variations add different ingredients: Italy often uses mozzarella and basil, Mexico adds salsa and avocado.
Ham sandwiches are frequently included in school lunch menus for children.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Ham provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Ham is rich in vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Ham contains iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood formation and bones.

items.title: Low carbohydrate option
items.content: When paired with whole‑grain bread, the sandwich can fit low‑carb diets.

items.title: Nutrient‑rich vegetables
items.content: Added veggies (tomato, lettuce, cucumber) supply vitamin C, fiber and antioxidants.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Ham is often salty; excess sodium may raise blood pressure.

items.title: Nitrates and preservatives
items.content: Some hams contain nitrates, which can be harmful in large amounts.

items.title: Fats and calories
items.content: The sandwich can be calorie‑dense, especially with mayonnaise and cheese.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The roll usually contains wheat; people with celiac disease should choose a gluten‑free option.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ham sandwiches are typically eaten cold, but they can be lightly toasted on a grill. Add fresh vegetables, mustard, or a light yogurt‑based sauce for balanced flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared sandwich in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours, wrapped in plastic film. Keep ham and the roll separate when possible to prevent the bread from becoming soggy.

content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice with carrots is a whole‑grain rice cooked together with grated carrots. The nutty flavor of the rice combined with the sweet taste of carrots makes the dish both nutritious and aromatic. It can be served as a side or as a main course.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice retains the bran and germ, providing more fiber and micronutrients than white rice.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts into vitamin A.
The rice‑carrot combination is common in many Asian cuisines for its flavor and bright color.
When stored properly, brown rice stays fresh for up to 6 months.
The high content of complex carbohydrates gives lasting satiety.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, helps maintain stable blood sugar levels, and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of vitamin A
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots supports vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium is essential for muscle and nerve function and helps regulate blood pressure.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Brown rice raises blood glucose slowly, which is beneficial for weight management and diabetes control.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Antioxidants from carrots help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid in whole grains can reduce the absorption of certain minerals if consumed in excess.

items.title: Carrot allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to carrots.

items.title: Potential arsenic accumulation
items.content: Brown rice can accumulate arsenic; it is advisable to vary grain sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rice and carrots as a side dish with meat, fish, or tofu. It can be added to salads, soups, or used as a base for vegetarian bowls. Cook rice with a 1:2 rice‑to‑water ratio, adding grated carrots 5‑10 minutes before the end of cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked rice should be kept in the refrigerator and consumed within 3‑4 days.
